item.title: 650 amputees to receive artificial limbs
item.description: MORE than 650 people in Fiji who have lost limbs are expected to regain their mobility through an India-funded artificial limb program scheduled to begin in October. India’s High Commissioner to Fiji Suneet Mehta said the Jaipur Foot Camp would provide artificial limbs to people who had been waiting for assistance following amputations over the past year.
item.content:encoded:
MORE than 650 people in Fiji who have lost limbs are expected to regain their mobility through an India-funded artificial limb program scheduled to begin in October.

India’s High Commissioner to Fiji Suneet Mehta said the Jaipur Foot Camp would provide artificial limbs to people who had been waiting for assistance following amputations over the past year.

He confirmed the camp would be conducted over two months in Suva, Nadi and Labasa, with between 15 and 20 people fitted with artificial limbs each day.

Mr Mehta said recipients would have their mobility restored within hours of arriving at the camp.

“It’s going to be a joyous feeling for the people who have lost their mobility.

“When they come in the morning, by the evening they will have their restored mobility.”

He said the program was another example of India’s support for Fiji’s healthcare sector.

Mr Mehta said the shipment of materials needed for the program was already on its way to Fiji.

“It should land and then get cleared, and then we should start the first week of October.”

He said the initiative would run throughout October and November in partnership with Fiji’s Ministry of Health to ensure those waiting for artificial limbs received assistance.

item.title: Meet reviews progress
item.description: FIJI is strengthening its planned relocation framework to protect communities living in climate-vulnerable areas. The Fijian Taskforce on the Relocation and Displacement of Communities Vulnerable to the Impacts of Climate Change convened its fourth-quarter meeting in Suva this week to review progress on planned relocation projects, climate mobility initiatives and future priorities.
item.content:encoded:
FIJI is strengthening its planned relocation framework to protect communities living in climate-vulnerable areas.

The Fijian Taskforce on the Relocation and Displacement of Communities Vulnerable to the Impacts of Climate Change convened its fourth-quarter meeting in Suva this week to review progress on planned relocation projects, climate mobility initiatives and future priorities.

The meeting brought together representatives from government ministries, development partners and invited observers to strengthen coordination and support a whole-of-government approach to climate-related relocation and displacement.

Chaired by the director for Climate Change Senivasa Waqairamasi the meeting endorsed in principle the Cultural Checklist for Planned Relocation in Fiji.

The checklist recognises the importance of protecting Fiji’s cultural values and traditions while ensuring the needs and voices of women and children are incorporated into relocation processes.

The Taskforce also progressed the Free, Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC) Guiding Framework, which will help strengthen community participation and ensure affected communities are meaningfully informed and involved in decisions concerning planned relocation.

Members further received updates on parametric insurance and heard from the International Organisation for Migration (IOM) on climate mobility initiatives and funding opportunities. These discussions reinforced the importance of partnerships in supporting safe, inclusive and people-centred approaches to planned relocation.

For Fiji, planned relocation is not simply about moving communities away from areas at risk. It is about protecting lives while preserving culture, identity, livelihoods and the deep connection communities have with the vanua.

The Government’s planned relocation framework therefore promotes processes that are transparent, inclusive, participatory and culturally appropriate, ensuring that communities affected by climate change remain at the centre of decisions about their future.

The Ministry of Environment and Climate Change acknowledged the continued support of German Agency for International Cooperation (GIZ)in advancing the work of the Taskforce and strengthening Fiji’s national approach to planned relocation.

Commissioner Western Apolosi Lewaqai raises a point during the 4th Quarter Meeting of the Fijian Taskforce on the Relocation and Displacement of Communities Vulnerable to the Impacts of Climate Change. Picture:SUPPLIED

item.title: ‘Need for more women in Parliament to help shape the nation’
item.description: INVESTING in women is an investment in society, and Fiji needs more women in Parliament to help shape the nation’s future, says Leader of the Opposition Inia Seruiratu. Delivering his speech at the the 14th Speaker’s Debate in Suva on Thursday, Mr Seruiratu said a message he heard during a meeting in Rome had reinforced his belief that women were essential to national development and decision-maki
item.content:encoded:
INVESTING in women is an investment in society, and Fiji needs more women in Parliament to help shape the nation’s future, says Leader of the Opposition Inia Seruiratu.

Delivering his speech at the the 14th Speaker’s Debate in Suva on Thursday, Mr Seruiratu said a message he heard during a meeting in Rome had reinforced his belief that women were essential to national development and decision-making.

“When we develop man, we are developing an individual but when we develop a woman, we are developing a society,” he said.

“Women, that is why we need you in Parliament. Because society needs you, that touch is missing, you are special and we need more of you in Parliament.”

He said the focus should shift from simply encouraging women to participate in politics to ensuring they were represented where national decisions were made.

“Enhancing women’s representation, not participation.”

“Enhancing women’s representation in political life is not a matter of equality. It is a prerequisite for more effective, more responsible, and sustainable decision-making that directly influences the development of our societies.”

“I wish to encourage all our women. We need more of women’s representation in Parliament. If we want to change laws, that is where it happens. If we want to influence, then we must participate.”

He said increasing women’s representation would strengthen governance and ensure Parliament better reflected the needs of all Fijians.

item.title: $940k upgrade – Plans for new-look Rakiraki market
item.description: RAKIRAKI Town is poised for major infrastructure improvements, with plans underway to expand its local market and upgrade the drainage system. Rakiraki Town Council Special Administrator Peni Duaniwai confirmed the upcoming developments, aimed to boost local commerce and enhance the region’s appeal to visitors.
item.content:encoded:
RAKIRAKI Town is poised for major infrastructure improvements, with plans underway to expand its local market and upgrade the drainage system.

Rakiraki Town Council Special Administrator Peni Duaniwai confirmed the upcoming developments, aimed to boost local commerce and enhance the region’s appeal to visitors.

“Rough estimate on the upgrade is $940,000 of the market, funding for the market project and the drainage system will be fully provided by the government but the drainage will have a different budget,” Mr Duaniwai said.

Town officials plan to begin construction in the new financial year to accommodate more local vendors and modernise facilities.

“We intend to start in the new financial year; it will accommodate more vendors and we are trying to raise the standard of our market for tourism purposes.”

He said the council was focusing heavily on sanitation and waste management to complement recent commercial growth along the coast, particularly within the tourism sector.

“Right now, there are more hotels built around the seaside and that’s one thing that we’re going to improve, the standard, and also the cleanliness of our town.”

In addition to town center upgrades, government authorities are evaluating long-term waste management options, including relocating the dump site.

“We just got our own landfill site and now, there is a plan from the government to move into somewhere in Vatukoula or Tavua but that is still in discussion stages now.”

item.title: Resort gifts new beds to RKS students
item.description: RADISSON Blu Resort Fiji on Denarau Island recently gifted 10 double bunk beds to government-owned Ratu Kadavulevu School (RKS) as part of the resort’s ongoing commitment to supporting local communities. Upon receiving information that the school’s Bure Cakau needed new beds, representatives from Radisson Blu Resort Fiji visited the school to identify how they could best assist.
item.content:encoded:
RADISSON Blu Resort Fiji on Denarau Island recently gifted 10 double bunk beds to government-owned Ratu Kadavulevu School (RKS) as part of the resort’s ongoing commitment to supporting local communities.

Upon receiving information that the school’s Bure Cakau needed new beds, representatives from Radisson Blu Resort Fiji visited the school to identify how they could best assist.

Speaking during the handover on Wednesday, RKS principal Joseva Jale expressed his sincere appreciation to the Radisson Blu Resort Fiji management and team.

“We have waited a long time for assistance, and today our prayers have finally been answered,” Mr Jale said.

“The children will now enjoy comfortable sleep, allowing them to focus better in class and dream bigger. We are truly grateful for this thoughtful donation.”

Parents who attended the presentation also shared their joy and gratitude, saying they were relieved to see that students enjoying new beds to call their own.

Radisson Blu Resort Fiji representative Nikotimasi Delai said the gifts reflected the resort’s belief that every child deserved a safe and comfortable place to rest.

“Our message is simple but important: the comfort and health of our students’ matter,” Mr Delai said.

“A clear mind starts with a rested body. Many of these students live far away from their families while pursuing their education.

“We hope these beds will provide not only comfort, but also support their health, wellbeing and ability to succeed in school,” he said.

The five-star resort on Denarau Island said it remains committed to making a positive impact in the communities it serves through meaningful partnerships and initiatives that improve the lives of children and families across Fiji.

item.title: Halle Berry praises Kokomo Private Island after Fiji family holiday
item.description: Hollywood actress Halle Berry has praised Fiji’s Kokomo Private Island and its staff after enjoying what she described as a memorable family vacation at the luxury resort. Berry shared her experience on social media, thanking the Kokomo team for their hospitality, warmth and attention to her family throughout their stay.
item.content:encoded:
Hollywood actress Halle Berry has praised Fiji’s Kokomo Private Island and its staff after enjoying what she described as a memorable family vacation at the luxury resort.

Berry shared her experience on social media, thanking the Kokomo team for their hospitality, warmth and attention to her family throughout their stay.

“This family vacation has been one for the ages!” Berry said.

She described everything at Kokomo as “sheer perfection”, saying the staff went out of their way to make the family feel welcome and cared for.

Berry gave special recognition to a staff member named Ima, who she said helped make the holiday particularly memorable.

According to the Academy Award-winning actress, Ima helped her son become dive certified, cared for her daughter when she experienced seasickness, encouraged Van to jump into a waterfall and even tended to Berry after she broke her toe while playing pickleball.

The family also managed to catch some fish during their island adventures.

“We will miss you most of all!” Berry told Ima.

A highlight of the Kokomo stay was a pre-birthday lovo celebration organised for Berry and her family.

Berry described the night as “epic”, praising the traditional island songs, local cuisine and warmth of the people who hosted the celebration.

“The sweet island songs you all sang and delicious cuisine paired with the biggest smiles I’ve ever seen made the night truly magical,” she said.

The actress also offered glowing praise for Fiji and its people following the experience.

“It’s true, Fiji does have the happiest people on Earth,” Berry said.

She ended her message by indicating that the family hoped their Kokomo experience would not be their last.

item.title: Police uproot more than 2,000 marijuana plants in North
item.description: Police have seized and destroyed more than 2,200 plants believed to be marijuana during separate anti-drug operations in Fiji’s Northern Division as authorities intensify efforts to dismantle illicit drug cultivation. Assistant Commissioner of Police Operations Kasiano Vusonilawe said officers from the Northern Division Operations team discovered and uprooted more than 2,000 suspected marijuana pl
item.content:encoded:
Police have seized and destroyed more than 2,200 plants believed to be marijuana during separate anti-drug operations in Fiji’s Northern Division as authorities intensify efforts to dismantle illicit drug cultivation.

Assistant Commissioner of Police Operations Kasiano Vusonilawe said officers from the Northern Division Operations team discovered and uprooted more than 2,000 suspected marijuana plants in the rugged Vatuyalewa mountain range.

In a separate operation, police also destroyed more than 200 green plants believed to be marijuana in the Nasea farming area in Tukavesi.

ACP Vusonilawe said those involved in cultivating marijuana had changed their methods in an attempt to avoid detection.

“The modus operandi of cultivators has changed, however, enhanced sharing of information and the use of drones has assisted with locating the farms in difficult terrains,” he said.

He said police remain committed to targeting the source of both marijuana and harder illicit drugs through sustained enforcement operations.

“Operations remain committed to getting to the source of both green and white drugs,” ACP Vusonilawe said.

He added that multiple arrests had been made over the past week across all five policing divisions for alleged unlawful possession of illicit drugs.

The operations have been supported by the Joint Task Force, which includes the Republic of Fiji Military Forces.

Police are continuing to urge members of the public to support the fight against drugs by reporting suspicious activity.

Anyone with information relating to drug offences is encouraged to contact the Police Drug Tip-Off Line on 1681.

item.title: One in three Fijian households struggle to cover expenses, RBF survey finds
item.description: One in three Fijian households do not earn enough to meet their regular expenses, while fewer than one in four people believe they are on track to achieve their financial goals, according to the Reserve Bank of Fiji’s 2025 Fiji Financial Services Demand Side Survey. The survey paints a sobering picture of household finances, showing that 33 per cent of households have incomes that fall short of th
item.content:encoded:
One in three Fijian households do not earn enough to meet their regular expenses, while fewer than one in four people believe they are on track to achieve their financial goals, according to the Reserve Bank of Fiji’s 2025 Fiji Financial Services Demand Side Survey.

The survey paints a sobering picture of household finances, showing that 33 per cent of households have incomes that fall short of their regular expenditure, while 46 per cent said their income was only enough to cover day-to-day expenses.

Only 18 per cent of households reported earning more than they spent.

The financial pressures were most pronounced in the Western Division, where 49 per cent of households said their income was insufficient to meet expenses, compared with 21 per cent in the Central Division.

Despite these challenges, 39 per cent of Fijians said they were always satisfied with their financial situation.

The survey also found that 55 per cent of adults said they set long-term financial goals and actively worked towards achieving them.

However, only 24 per cent considered themselves on track to reach those goals, while 52 per cent said they were making some progress.

Around one in five respondents admitted they had lost track of their financial goals because of competing financial commitments.

The report also highlighted the limited financial resilience of many households.

If they were to lose their main source of income, 61 per cent of respondents said they could survive for one month or less, including 28 per cent who could manage for only one week or less.

Only 10 per cent believed they could meet their living expenses for six months or longer without their primary income.

When running short of money, the most common response was to cut household spending, followed by using savings or seeking help from family and friends.

In the event of an unexpected financial emergency, 47 per cent said they would borrow from family or friends, while 44 per cent would rely on their personal savings.

Older people, people living with disabilities and those excluded from formal financial services were more likely to depend on relatives and friends for financial support than on savings.

The survey also found that fewer than half of Fijians seek financial advice, with those who do most commonly turning to household members, relatives or friends for guidance.

The findings suggest that while financial inclusion has improved significantly in Fiji, many households continue to face financial pressure, limited savings and little capacity to withstand unexpected economic shocks.
